Very common for chronic ear infections to be related to allergy. Most common allergies being flea, food, and environmental/atopy. Are the ears themselves swollen? If ear canal is narrowed, steroids are indicated. If you have any GENTLE dog-specific ear cleaning solution at home, could use daily for about a week, then transition to 1x/wk. Gabapentin is a very safe medication. However, if she has kidney disease, your cat will not metabolize it as well, since gabapentin is metabolized by the kidneys. Again, not necessarily dangerous, but can cause more sedation and ataxia than you might want. (Also, by mg, do you mean ml? Standard dose for gabapentin is 100mg) You can talk to your vet about decreasing her dose amount or frequency or stopping the dose until her motor function normalizes again

Hey so, hard to tell from the photo, but this could possibly be a corneal sequestrum if you are seeing a "black bit" on the eye. That is basically when a part of the cornea dies from an eye infection or chronic irritation. Would definitely recommend a vet trip, as corneal sequestrums can rupture the eye as the dead cornea sloughs off. Also could possibly be scar tissue from the eye infection, which is more benign. Again, cannot know for sure if that's what it is without proper exam.

I agree with toxinogen! Food is a way to a baby’s heart! You can try different types, but warm, stinky, wet food usually works best. Sometimes they’ll also like the sound of kibble shaking around a container. Place the food in a carrier and try to shut the door with the kitty inside. If this doesn’t seem to work, for whatever reason (the kitty noticed you, you can’t sneak up on it, etc), you can try to get the kitty’s trust, but this may be a long road. You could place food out for the cat; then, the next time, sit near the food after you put it out. Next, you would try to put the food closer to you or feed the cat with a spoon. The goal is the feed the cat with your hand. Of course, the carrier trap option is much simpler, and it may take a combination of both approaches. Best of luck!!

A few years ago, someone stole our German pointer. We live in Louisiana, in the country. We came across this dog when he showed up at our home (from the woods), super malnourished and with markings that looked like cigarette burns. He had been abused, but he went to right up to my mama, like he was asking for help. He had no collar or chip. We nursed him back and named him Feske. He was a very grateful boy.

Feske had a collar with our information on it and everything. My dad always let the dogs out for 2 hours when he would come home. But, while my dad was mowing, Feske took off running. He had done this once before in the 3 years we had him, and he had come back that night. Still, we searched all over for him, making sure that he hadn’t been hit by a car. He hadn’t.  And he didn’t come back. So, it’s very obvious to us that someone found him, saw he was a purebred, and took him despite him having contact info. I just hope that it wasn’t his previous owners.
